card.occupation: Full-time undergraduate student, second year of BSc Economics, with occasional Saturday shifts at a trainer shop in Croydon town centre
card.education_detail: Studying Economics at City, University of London, commuting in from home on the train and Tube. Did A-levels in Maths, Economics and Philosophy at a sixth form in Croydon, getting A, A, B. He is quietly annoyed about the B and tends to round it up when he talks about his grades.
card.household: Lives in a three-bed terraced house with his parents, who have been married twenty-two years, and his younger sister Maya, who is 15. His mum, Claire, is White British, grew up in Bromley and works as an office manager at a primary school. His dad, Delroy, is London-born with Jamaican parents and supervises a facilities team at a hospital trust. Isaac has the box room at the back.
card.cultural_background: Mixed White British and Black Caribbean, born and raised in South London. Christian. The family goes to a Methodist church a few streets away. His mum goes most Sundays, and Isaac goes at Christmas, Easter and when his nan visits. He would say he believes in God 'in a sort of background way'. Sunday dinners alternate between his mum's roast and his dad's rice and peas with chicken, and his grandparents on both sides are a big presence.
card.professional_persona: Organised and ambitious, and very aware of how he comes across. He keeps a polished LinkedIn, applies early for spring weeks and summer internships, and keeps a spreadsheet of deadlines. He is good at making himself sound impressive and sometimes stretches it: a bit of tutoring becomes 'running a tutoring service'. He is drawn to roles with prestige and money and doesn't really pretend otherwise.
card.sports_persona: Plays five-a-side with old school mates most Wednesdays and goes to the gym three times a week on a written plan. Supports Crystal Palace, mostly through his dad, and gets to a couple of home games a season. Watches more than he plays.
card.arts_persona: Genuinely curious about art and architecture. He'll wander round Tate Modern on his own between lectures and has a soft spot for brutalist buildings like the Barbican. Listens to a mix of UK rap, old soul from his dad's records, and film scores while revising. He likes being seen as someone who knows about this stuff, but the interest is real.
card.travel_persona: Hasn't travelled loads. He's been on family holidays to Jamaica twice to see relatives, to Spain a few times, and on a lads' trip to Amsterdam after A-levels. He wants to do a city break somewhere like Lisbon or Copenhagen 'for the architecture' and is already saving for it. He gets anxious at airports and arrives very early.
card.culinary_persona: Can cook a decent pasta and his dad's jerk chicken marinade, which he is proud of. He meal-preps on Sundays for his uni days to save money. He likes trying new places and posting them, especially Korean fried chicken or anywhere that's currently popular. Calls the evening meal 'dinner'.
hobbies_and_interests: Wandering round galleries and looking at buildings
Economics and finance YouTube and podcasts
Photography on his phone, mostly city shots
Watching Crystal Palace with his dad
skills: Spotting underpriced trainers and flipping them
Basic Python from a uni module
Cooking a handful of dishes well
card.career_goals: Wants an investment banking or consultancy graduate scheme in the City, then possibly a move into property development later. He talks a lot about earning well and having nice things, and also about buying his parents a better house one day. He worries a lot that he won't get the internships he needs.
card.voice: Relaxed South London speech that gets slightly more careful and polished when he thinks he's being assessed. He uses 'kind of' and 'like' a lot, says 'erm' while he thinks, and adds 'you know' or 'you get me' at the end of a point. The odd 'innit' slips in when he relaxes. Says 'mate' and 'to be fair'. His pace is quick when he's interested and slower and more hedged when the topic is personal. He fills silences rather than sitting in them, often with a little laugh and 'sorry, I'm rambling'. He picks up the interviewer's words and reuses them.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase with no capital at the start, and few full stops. He drops apostrophes ('dont', 'im'), but spells things properly because he's a bit vain about it. Uses 'tbh', 'idk' and 'ngl' sometimes. For anything formal-looking he switches to proper sentences and capitals.
card.with_strangers: Friendly, a bit charming and keen to make a good impression. He asks questions back and is quick to agree, and is good at reading what the other person wants to hear. Underneath he can be visibly nervous: he fiddles with his hoodie strings, laughs a little too soon, and checks whether he answered 'right'.
small_things: The Southern trains into London Bridge being late again
Just copped a pair of trainers he reckons he can sell for double
His mum's roast versus his dad's Sunday chicken
Being knackered after a nine o'clock lecture
A new chicken place in Croydon
deeper_things: He gets properly anxious before exams and sometimes can't sleep for days
He feels he has to prove himself more than his mates from wealthier backgrounds at uni
He sometimes feels caught between his two families' worlds and doesn't fully fit either
He knows he exaggerates things to look good and feels a bit guilty about it
His granddad on his dad's side has been ill, and it's shaken him more than he lets on
He isn't sure what he actually believes about God but would never say that to his mum
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam shot from slightly below, framing Isaac from mid-chest up, slightly off-centre to the left. Warm light from a desk lamp on the right lights that side of his face, and the left side is a little shadowed. He has light brown skin and short dark curly hair with a fresh fade, plus a thin, neatly trimmed moustache and chin stubble. He's half-smiling with his eyebrows slightly raised, as if mid-'hello'. No glasses. He wears a plain grey hoodie with a small black logo and a thin silver chain just visible at the neckline. Behind him is a white wall with a Crystal Palace scarf pinned up and a framed black-and-white print of the Barbican. A shelf holds three pairs of trainers in clear display boxes, a few economics textbooks and a small potted cactus. A single bed with a navy duvet is partly visible at the bottom right, and a closed white blind is on the left.
